title: Share of Variation in Outcomes Explained
source: Michigan Surveys of Consumers; electionlib; FRED. Q3 sentiment reading; author's calculations.
note: In-sample R² from OLS regressions of the incumbent party's vote share on each set of predictors. 'Economics' is a Fair-like model (GDP growth, inflation, and incumbency terms); 'confidence' is the level and year-over-year change in Q3 consumer sentiment. Confidence alone explains a large share of the variation, and the economic terms add incremental fit — more so for presidential years. In-sample R² flatters small samples; the out-of-sample horse race tells a more cautious story.
